title: Exercise (C2: Newton’s form of the interpolant)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(c_0, \dots, c_n \in F\) be distinct. Put \(N_0 = 1\) and \(N_k = (x - c_0)(x - c_1) \cdots (x - c_{k-1})\) for \(1 \le k \le n + 1\) . Prove that \((N_0, \dots, N_n)\) is a basis of \(F[x]_{\le n}\) . Let \(p = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_kN_k\) . Show that \(p(c_i) = \sum_{k=0}^{i} a_kN_k(c_i)\) and \(N_i(c_i) \ne 0\) . Explain why the coefficients \(a_0, a_1, \dots\) of the interpolant can be found one at a time, and show that \(a_0 = y_0\) and \(a_1 = \frac{y_1 - y_0}{c_1 - c_0}\) . Let \(p_n \in F[x]_{\le n}\) interpolate \(y_0, \dots, y_n\) at \(c_0, \dots, c_n\) , and let \(c_{n+1}\) be a further node, distinct from the others, with a value \(y_{n+1}\) . Prove that the interpolant \(p_{n+1} \in F[x]_{\le n+1}\) is \[ p_{n+1} = p_n + \frac{y_{n+1} - p_n(c_{n+1})}{N_{n+1}(c_{n+1})}\,N_{n+1} . \] Find the Newton form of the interpolant of @exr-interpolation-and-crt-b1 , and then the interpolant after adding the point \((4, 0)\) . Why is this more economical than recomputing with Lagrange’s formula? Hint: for (c), check the values of the right-hand side at all \(n + 2\) nodes.

title: Lemma 5.6.3 (Coprime to Each, Coprime to the Product)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(p, q_1, \dots, q_s \in F[x]\) . If \(p\) is coprime to each \(q_j\) , then there are \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \(ap + b\,q_1 \cdots q_s = 1\) , and \(p\) is coprime to \(q_1 \cdots q_s\) . Let \(m_1, \dots, m_k \in F[x]\) be non-zero and pairwise coprime , that is, \(\gcd(m_i, m_j) = 1\) whenever \(i \ne j\) . If \(m_i \mid h\) for every \(i\) , then \(m_1 \cdots m_k \mid h\) .

title: Theorem 5.6.6 (CRT as an Isomorphism)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m_1, \dots, m_k \in F[x]\) be non-zero and pairwise coprime, and put \(m = m_1 \cdots m_k\) . Then \[ \Phi \colon F[x]/\langle m \rangle \to F[x]/\langle m_1 \rangle \times \dots \times F[x]/\langle m_k \rangle, \qquad f + \langle m \rangle \mapsto \bigl(f + \langle m_1 \rangle, \dots, f + \langle m_k \rangle\bigr), \] is a well-defined isomorphism of vector spaces.

title: Theorem 5.6.4 (Chinese Remainder Theorem for Polynomials)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m_1, \dots, m_k \in F[x]\) be non-zero and pairwise coprime, and put \(m = m_1 \cdots m_k\) . For all \(r_1, \dots, r_k \in F[x]\) : there is \(f \in F[x]\) with \(f \equiv r_i \pmod{m_i}\) for every \(i\) ; if \(f\) and \(g\) both satisfy (a), then \(f \equiv g \pmod{m}\) ; there is exactly one such \(f\) with \(\deg f < \deg m\) .

title: Theorem 5.6.5 (Dimension of F[x]/\langle m \rangle)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m \in F[x]\) be non-zero of degree \(d\) . Then \(F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) is finite-dimensional with \[ \dim F[x]/\langle m \rangle = \deg m = d . \] If \(d \ge 1\) , the cosets \((1 + \langle m \rangle, x + \langle m \rangle, \dots, x^{d-1} + \langle m \rangle)\) form a basis.

title: Theorem 5.6.1 (Lagrange Interpolation)
page: 5.6 Interpolation and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) , let \(c_0, \dots, c_n \in F\) be distinct, and let \((\ell_0, \dots, \ell_n)\) be the Lagrange basis for these nodes. \(\ell_i(c_j) = \delta_{ij}\) for all \(i, j \in \{0, \dots, n\}\) . \((\ell_0, \dots, \ell_n)\) is a basis of \(F[x]_{\le n}\) , and every \(p \in F[x]_{\le n}\) satisfies \[ p = \sum_{i=0}^{n} p(c_i)\,\ell_i . \] For all \(y_0, \dots, y_n \in F\) , the unique \(p \in F[x]_{\le n}\) with \(p(c_i) = y_i\) for every \(i\) is \[ p = \sum_{i=0}^{n} y_i\,\ell_i . \]

title: Definition 5.7.1 (Annihilating Polynomial)
content: Let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . A polynomial \(p \in F[x]\) annihilates \(T\) if \(p(T) = 0\) , the zero operator on \(V\) .

title: Example (Finding an Annihilating Polynomial)
content: Find a non-zero polynomial of least possible degree that annihilates \(B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ)\) .

title: Example (Two Ways to Evaluate)
content: Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(\nQ)\) . Compute \(p(A)\) for \(p = x^2 - 4x + 4\) and \(q = x^2 - 3x\) , once by expanding and once by factoring.

title: Example (A Splitting with a Repeated Factor)
content: Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ)\) . Verify that \(A^2(A - I_3) = 0\) , and use @thm-kernel-splitting with \(p = x^2\) , \(q = x - 1\) to split \(\nQ^3\) , giving both projections as polynomials in \(A\) .

title: Example (Recovering the Involution Decomposition)
content: Let \(F\) have characteristic not \(2\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) with \(T^2 = \id_V\) . Apply @thm-kernel-splitting with \(p = x - 1\) and \(q = x + 1\) , and compare with @thm-involution-decomposition . What goes wrong in characteristic \(2\) ?

title: Example (Recovering Projections and Direct Sums)
content: Let \(P \in \cL(V)\) be a projection. Apply @thm-kernel-splitting with \(p = x\) and \(q = x - 1\) , and compare with @thm-projection-direct-sum (a).

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State what it means that \(p \mapsto p(T)\) is linear and multiplicative. True or false: if \(p(T)\,q(T) = 0\) , then \(p(T) = 0\) or \(q(T) = 0\) . Justify your answer. Why does every operator on a finite-dimensional space have a non-zero annihilating polynomial? Is the same true on \(F[x]\) ? True or false: if \(p\) annihilates \(T\) and \(p \mid q\) , then \(q\) annihilates \(T\) . Justify your answer. State the kernel splitting lemma for \((pq)(T) = 0\) , and say where coprimality is used in its proof. True or false: for every subspace \(U\) of \(V\) and every \(T \in \cL(V)\) , \(T\) maps \(U\) into \(U\) . Justify your answer.

title: Exercise (B1: A polynomial of a 2 \times 2 matrix)
content: Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_2(\nQ)\) . Compute \(p(A)\) for \(p = x^2 - 7\) and for \(q = x^2 + x - 5\) . Hence show that \(A\) is invertible and find \(A^{-1}\) as a polynomial in \(A\) .

title: Exercise (B2: An annihilating polynomial by elimination)
content: Let \(C = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nQ)\) . Compute \(C^2\) and \(C^3\) , and show that \((I_3, C, C^2)\) is linearly independent. Find a linear dependence among \(I_3, C, C^2, C^3\) , and hence a monic polynomial \(p\) of degree \(3\) with \(p(C) = 0\) . Hence show that \(C\) is invertible and write \(C^{-1}\) as a polynomial in \(C\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Operators with T^3 = T)
content: Let \(F\) have characteristic not \(2\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) with \(T^3 = T\) . Use @thm-kernel-splitting with \(p = x\) and \(q = x^2 - 1\) to show \(V = \ker T \oplus \ker(T^2 - \id_V)\) , with projection \(\id_V - T^2\) onto \(\ker T\) . Show that \(V = \ker T \oplus \ker(T - \id_V) \oplus \ker(T + \id_V)\) . Verify that the projections onto the three summands in (b) are \(\id_V - T^2\) , \(\tfrac12(T^2 + T)\) and \(\tfrac12(T^2 - T)\) , in the sense that these three operators sum to \(\id_V\) and each maps \(V\) into the corresponding kernel.

title: Exercise (C1: Inverses are polynomials)
content:
Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) and \(T \in \cL(V)\) . Suppose \(p(T) = 0\) for some \(p \in F[x]\) with \(p(0)

title: Exercise (C2: Splitting with k coprime factors)
content: Let \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and let \(p_1, \dots, p_k \in F[x]\) be non-zero and pairwise coprime, with \(k \ge 2\) . Put \(p = p_1 \cdots p_k\) and \(W = \ker p(T)\) . Use @thm-crt-polynomials to find \(e_1, \dots, e_k \in F[x]\) with \(e_i \equiv 1 \pmod{p_i}\) and \(e_i \equiv 0 \pmod{p_j}\) for \(j \ne i\) . Show that \(p \mid e_1 + \dots + e_k - 1\) and that \(p \mid p_ie_i\) for each \(i\) . Prove that for every \(\w \in W\) , \(\w = e_1(T)\w + \dots + e_k(T)\w\) with \(e_i(T)\w \in \ker p_i(T)\) . Prove that \(W = \ker p_1(T) \oplus \dots \oplus \ker p_k(T)\) , and that \(e_i(T)\) is the identity on \(\ker p_i(T)\) and zero on \(\ker p_j(T)\) for \(j \ne i\) . Deduce: if \(p(T) = 0\) , then \(V = \ker p_1(T) \oplus \dots \oplus \ker p_k(T)\) , and the projection onto the \(i\) -th summand along the others is the polynomial \(e_i(T)\) . Hint: for the second divisibility in (a), use @lem-coprime-product (b).

title: Exercise (C3: The same rotation over \nR and over \nC)
content:
Let \(A =  egin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\) , so that \(A^2 + I_2 = 0\) . Over \(
C\) , apply @thm-kernel-splitting to \(T_A\) on \(
C^2\) with \(p = x - i\) and \(q = x + i\) . Find both kernels and write the projection onto \(\ker(A - iI_2)\) as a polynomial in \(A\) . Over \(
R\) , show that the only subspaces of \(

title: Theorem 5.7.2 (Every Operator Satisfies a Polynomial)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) with \(\dim V = n\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . Then there is a non-zero \(p \in F[x]\) with \(\deg p \le n^2\) and \(p(T) = 0\) . The same holds for every \(A \in M_n(F)\) .

title: Theorem 5.7.3 (The Annihilating Polynomials Form an Ideal)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) and \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and let \[ I_T \coloneqq \{ p \in F[x] : p(T) = 0 \}. \] \(I_T\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) . Either \(I_T = \{0\}\) , or there is a unique monic \(m \in F[x]\) with \(I_T = \langle m \rangle\) . In the second case, for every \(p \in F[x]\) , \[ p(T) = 0 \iff m \mid p , \] and \(m\) has the least degree among the non-zero polynomials annihilating \(T\) . If \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \(I_T \ne \{0\}\) , and \(\deg m \le (\dim V)^2\) .

title: Theorem 5.7.1 (Evaluation at an Operator)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) and \(T \in \cL(V)\) . Then the map \[ F[x] \to \cL(V), \qquad p \mapsto p(T), \] has the following properties. It is linear : \((cp + q)(T) = c\,p(T) + q(T)\) for all \(p, q \in F[x]\) and \(c \in F\) . It is multiplicative and sends \(1\) to \(\id_V\) : \((pq)(T) = p(T)\,q(T)\) and \(1(T) = \id_V\) . Its image \(\{ p(T) : p \in F[x] \}\) is a subspace of \(\cL(V)\) , closed under composition, in which any two operators commute. If \(S \in \cL(V)\) commutes with \(T\) , then \(S\) commutes with \(p(T)\) for every \(p \in F[x]\) .

title: Theorem 5.7.4 (T Preserves Kernels and Images of Polynomials in T)
content: Let \(R, S \in \cL(V)\) with \(SR = RS\) . Then \(S\v \in \ker R\) for every \(\v \in \ker R\) , and \(S\w \in \im R\) for every \(\w \in \im R\) . In particular, for \(T \in \cL(V)\) and \(p, q \in F[x]\) , the operator \(q(T)\) maps \(\ker p(T)\) into \(\ker p(T)\) and \(\im p(T)\) into \(\im p(T)\) . Taking \(q = x\) : \(T\) maps \(\ker p(T)\) and \(\im p(T)\) into themselves.

title: Theorem 5.7.5 (Kernel Splitting Lemma)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , let \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and let \(p, q \in F[x]\) be coprime . Choose \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \(ap + bq = 1\) ( @cor-bezout-polynomials ), and put \[ W = \ker (pq)(T), \qquad E_1 = b(T)\,q(T), \qquad E_2 = a(T)\,p(T). \] Then: \(W = \ker p(T) \oplus \ker q(T)\) ; \(E_1 + E_2 = \id_V\) , and for every \(\w \in W\) , the splitting of \(\w\) in (a) is \[ \w = E_1\w + E_2\w, \qquad E_1\w \in \ker p(T), \quad E_2\w \in \ker q(T); \] so \(E_1\) maps \(W\) into \(W\) and acts on \(W\) as the projection onto \(\ker p(T)\) along \(\ker q(T)\) , and \(E_2\) acts on \(W\) as the projection onto \(\ker q(T)\) along \(\ker p(T)\) ; in particular, if \((pq)(T) = 0\) , then \[ V = \ker p(T) \oplus \ker q(T), \] and the projections of \(V\) onto the two summands along each other are the polynomials \((bq)(T)\) and \((ap)(T)\) in \(T\) .
